item.title: Marvel Studios has revealed a new Avengers: Doomsday poster, giving audiences a closer look not only at Doctor Doom but also at the three Latverian witches who will accompany him this December.
item.description:
Marvel Studios has revealed a new Avengers: Doomsday poster, giving audiences a closer look not only at Doctor Doom but also at the three Latverian witches who will accompany him this December.
This latest look at the new Marvel Cinematic Universe movie was shared on social media as part of this weekend's San Diego Comic-Con Málaga in Spain. It was an event that saw stars like Anthony Mackie, Winston Duke, and David Harbor make an appearance, with this latest look coming arriving as a little more than a high-res look at Robert Downey Jr.'s take on a classic comic book villain.
Doctor Doom takes center stage in the new Avengers: Doomsday poster. He's looking as menacing as ever, striking a pose similar to the one we've seen before but with somewhat better lighting. The real highlight from the new poster, however, is the three Latverian witches standing behind him.
These three witches – and their hidden identities – have been the subject of much debate amongst MCU fans the last few months. These same mystery characters brought their purple, red, and green robes to San Diego Comic-Con in California this past July. The average onlooker might assume these characters will be little more than henchmen to be discarded in a massive CGI fight sequence, but some aren't so convinced.
Warning! Potential Avengers: Doomsday spoilers follow.
Many believe the faces behind these cold metal masks may be ones we've seen before. Prominent theories suspect the witch with the red robes could be Elizabeth Olsen's Wanda Maximoff, with the green-robed witch's secret identity being Loki show alum Sophia Di Martino's Sylvie.
While not everyone has landed on the same answer for these aforementioned witches, fans are truly split when it comes to who the character wearing the purple robe is. Some say it's Kathryn Hahn's Agatha Harkness, while others believe it's Charlize Theron's Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness cameo character, Clea.
As these are all just theories for now, there's always the chance all three Latverian witches could be nothing more than Doom drones for the Avengers to fight through. Still, recent developments in the MCU have led some to believe Avengers: Doomsday has some secret cameos it's saving for theaters.
Meanwhile, Mackie took his Comic-Con appearance as an opportunity to tease some of the most surprising moments from the new movie. X/Twitter user @CatherineComTH captured and shared the moment online.
"I think the big thing is the amount of doom you're going to see," he said when asked what people will be most surprised by. "Every corner we turn and every time somebody speaks, it's like, 'There's a lot of doom outside.' It's non-stop pandemonium.
"The best part about that is what the Russo brothers are great at: giving every character and every person their moment. Every time I go to watch Endgame, every single character was given their moment for the audience to connect with them and grieve with them. I think it's the same in this movie. You just have so many people."
All will be revealed when Avengers: Doomsday arrives December 18, 2026. Until then, you can see what directors Joe and Anthony Russo had to say about the film's runtime. You can also read what Nightcrawler actor Alan Cumming said regarding his lack of understanding of the movie's plot.

item.title: Inde Navarrette has opened up about playing Rogue in X-Men, saying she's "doing everything humanly possible" to make sure she does the character justice.
item.description:
Inde Navarrette has opened up about playing Rogue in X-Men, saying she's "doing everything humanly possible" to make sure she does the character justice.
The Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) X-Men reboot movie has a lot to live up to. For better or worse, previous films in the mutant-centered corner of the Marvel universe spent decades establishing characters like Cyclops and Rogue, and now, Navarrette is one of a few actors set to shake everything up.
The actress, who was picked to play the power-siphoning superhero earlier this year, told the LA Times that she's not taking her role in the reboot lightly. In fact, she's doing anything but.
"I'm doing everything humanly possible because I love that character," Navarrette said. "I've studied that character. I want to do it justice for myself, for [director Jake Schrieier], for what they want to portray and also for what I as a fan want her to be like. I’m doing everything, exclamation point."
Having parts in shows like 13 Reasons Why and Superman & Lois means Navarrette has been on TV screens for years, but her role as Nikki in low-budget horror phenomenon Obsession took her fame to a new level. Through all of the Oscar buzz and turned-down parts, it was Schreier's X-Men she decided to sign on to for one of her first post-Obsession roles.
Playing Rogue in X-Men means stepping into the shoes of a character with decades of history. Aside from the Mississippi-born mutant's history in comics, she's also already appeared in numerous animated and live-action projects, with actress Anna Paquin portraying her in films like the 2000 X-Men movie and X2: X-Men United.
Meanwhile, Navarrette also recently teased some of the steps she's taking just to make sure she nails Rogue's unforgettable southern accent. While she preps for what could be the biggest role of her career, she's already got a few notable names in her corner. Last month, Lenore Zann, the voice of Rogue in multiple animated X-Men projects through the years, offered her support to the Marvel newcomer.
Navarette will take the reins – but not until 2028. The MCU X-Men Movie is currently slated to premiere May 5 of that year, and when it does, it will introduce a collection of other new actors to play familiar characters. The full list includes Navarrette as Rogue, Adam Driver as Mister Sinister, Maya Boyd as Storm, Christopher Abbott as Professor X, Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Kit Connor as Cyclops, Samara Weaving as Emma Frost, and Asa Germann as Angel. Details about its plot remain under wraps, but Schreier has teased some of the comic book stories that will inspire its story.
In the meantime, some of the previous X-Men are set to return to the big screen when Avengers: Doomsday marks the beginning of the end for another MCU saga this December. With Avengers: Secret Wars set to arrive the following year, there's no telling which other heroes will make an appearance in the near future.

item.title: RuneFest 2026 is over, and we’ve got a roundup of everything announced at Jagex’s big show celebrating its long-running fantasy MMORPG.
item.description:
RuneFest 2026 is over, and we’ve got a roundup of everything announced at Jagex’s big show celebrating its long-running fantasy MMORPG.
This year saw a number of significant announcements, none bigger than confirmation that a fourth RuneScape MMO is in the works. Jagex hasn’t officially called it RuneScape 4 (RS4 is the working title), but we know it’s built on Unreal Engine and is designed to use the latest technology and design, so it really does sound like a next-gen RuneScape game. There’s no information on when it will be released, but the teaser trailer is below.
Jagex announced a new RuneScape animated adaptation, in partnership with YouTuber Charlie White, aka MoistCr1TiKaL, and production company Lyrical Media. No word on what this is exactly or when it will be released, but it’s happening!
Jagex announced RuneScape Reignited, which launches December 2. Jagex called it a “defining moment” for the 25-year-old game, designed to rekindle interest among lapsed players and get existing players excited. There’s a Remastered Journey and Adventure Guide, a fresh economy, and brand-new hi scores. Players can get full Reignited Access without membership from December 2-12. The long-awaited Plugin API launches this month, with players getting an early hands-on ahead of official release. The debut trailer is below:
We also got what Jagex called “the biggest roadmap in the game’s history.” 2027 content unfolds in three story arcs, all of which tie into long-running storylines. Hoard of Dragons (January) offers a sequel to the popular Dragon Slayer quest, City of Gnomes continues the gnome storyline, and Secrets of Karamja introduces a new endgame raid. Also coming is an Agility skill rework, new skilling and solo bosses, new area expansions, and a new Grandmaster Quest.
Old School RuneScape, meanwhile, got an updated roadmap. The Golden Gates to Menaphos are opening finally after 20 years, alongside a suite of fan-demanded content. The Fractured Archive, a new endgame raid, launches October 20. Hardcore Worlds launches November 4. And next year will also see the continuation of the Fairytale questline, Quest month, Dungeons of Gielinor, a Mining and Smithing rework, Chosen Commander, and the Tower of Xorphoros.
The recently released spinoff, RuneScape: Dragonwilds, saw the announcement of the Blood Crystal Saga and updated plans for 2027. The Luminance update is a prelude to 2027’s Blood Crystal Saga, and launches in December this year. This features the introduction of the Elves into RuneScape: Dragonwilds, new elven-themed customisation options for player characters and buildings alike and the Prayer skill.
The Blood Crystal Saga kicks off in 2027 starting with the Song of Rebellion in early 2027. These updates feature enemies like Moss Giants, Kebbits, and Implings, the Hunter Skill as well as new areas for players to explore, new quests and gear as well new decorations for houses inspired by the classic RuneScape city of Prifddinas.
Expect quarterly updates, which will include new Skills such as Hunter and Slayer, as well as monthly updates featuring side quests, weapons, decorations and quality of life improvements. Official modding arrives on Dragonwilds in 2027 through a new partnership with CurseForge — complete with dedicated creation tools and an in-game mod browser and installer, available across all platforms including console.

item.title: Developer Jagex has announced a fourth MMO in the long-running RuneScape franchise, as well as an animated adaptation.
item.description:
Developer Jagex has announced a fourth MMO in the long-running RuneScape franchise, as well as an animated adaptation.
At RuneFest in Birmingham, England, Jagex offered a glimpse at this new MMO, which it said was built “for a new generation of players.” It’s still in early development (a release isn't expected for at least a few years), and it doesn’t have an official title (Jagex is going with RS4 as a working title for now), but it will “bring the world of Gielinor to life in Unreal Engine, combining the depth, freedom and community-led spirit that have defined RuneScape for 25 years with the technology and game design possibilities of today.”
Jagex currently operates RuneScape itself, Old School RuneScape, and spinoff RuneScape: Dragonwilds. RuneScape has seen a number of major updates tied to sequel names, including a rename to RuneScape 2 in 2004 and RuneScape 3 in 2013. But both were dropped in favor of, simply, RuneScape, and it is now treated as an ongoing live service. It's tempting, then, to call this new game RuneScape 4, and it may end up justifying the name, but Jagex has yet to rubber stamp any title.
Indeed, we hardly know anything about this new RuneScape MMO, but with the mention of Unreal Engine, the expectation is it will have modern visuals and design. An image from the concept teaser and the concept teaser itself are below.
Here's the official blurb on the fourth RuneScape MMO:
In a blog post, Jagex explained that it has announced RuneScape 4 so early because it wants to build on the tech development it made for Dragonwilds, and lean on the community co-development it established through RuneScape and Old School. The developer insisted RS4 is not a replacement for either RuneScape, Old School, or Dragonwilds, each of which has its own dedicated team and will continue to see investment. "We’ll be designing RS4 to sit alongside them as an additional way to experience RuneScape and the world of Gielinor," Jagex said.
"In fact, we think having different RuneScape experiences can make the whole family stronger," the developer continued. "Players may spend most of their time in one game, move between several, or discover Gielinor for the very first time through RS4. The ambition isn't to replace the RuneScape games you love. It's to make the RuneScape universe bigger."
Jagex also confirmed RS4 will be set in Gielinor, as you'd expect, and in the Sixth Age. "But we're beginning somewhere that RuneScape players have only recently started to discover - and that is Ashenfall. An area first explored in RuneScape: Dragonwilds, and a landmass to the north-east of the Gielinor.
"RS4 will take place years after the events of Dragonwilds and the destruction of the Dragon Queen Kuldra. Time has passed, the world has moved on, and Ashenfall has changed with it. But Ashenfall is only the beginning.
"Our ambition is for this adventure to grow far beyond Ashenfall over time, moving into places you know and love, as well as opening up new places and stories across Gielinor."
RuneScape is of course one of the longest-running video games in the world. Jagex says it’s seen over 300 million player accounts created in the 25 years since RuneScape first launched. But the company’s plan is to expand the franchise into new genres and even adaptations. For example, at RuneFest Jagex also announced work had started on a new RuneScape animated adaption, in partnership with YouTuber Charlie White, aka MoistCr1TiKaL, and LA-based production company Lyrical Media. Here’s the official blurb:
Jagex announced a lot more at RuneFest today. Here’s everything we saw.

item.title: The Gears of War: E-Day developers at The Coalition say they are "proud to be one of Xbox's main titles" as Microsoft refocuses on exclusivity.
item.description:
The Gears of War: E-Day developers at The Coalition say they are "proud to be one of Xbox's main titles" as Microsoft refocuses on exclusivity.
Studio art director Aryan Hanbeck and creative director Matt Searcy opened up about The Coalition's place in the Xbox portfolio during an interview with gaming news content creator Destin Lergarie (via MP1st). Searcy said he and the rest of the team were "proud" when asked how they feel about Gears of War: E-Day's status as an Xbox exclusive.
"Well, we feel great because Gears has such a long, storied… It's part of Xbox's DNA. It's woven into it," he said. "At The Coalition, we feel pretty honored to have Gears and be the ones bringing that legacy forward. We know how much it means to people. We know how much it means to us."
Gears of War: E-Day is firmly a console exclusive, but there was a lot of confusion surrounding which platforms Gears of War: E-Day would be available on as recently as four months ago. The once-Xbox-exclusive franchise made its debut on PlayStation consoles when original remaster, Gears of War: Reloaded, released in August 2025. Many took its presence on PS5 as a sign not only that the series would continue to come to Sony's console but also that the days of exclusive titles may nearly be behind us – and for a while, that seemed to be the case.
Leaked listings and rumors were officially shut down at the Xbox Games Showcase 2026 when Xbox CEO Asha Sharma proudly declared that Marcus Fenix and Dom Santiago's Emergence Day prequel story would only be coming to Xbox Series X/S and PC. It was a shock decision that arrived as the Microsoft gaming entity kicked off a broader push for more exclusive games. Perhaps even more shocking at the time were the announcements that immediately followed, including the company's promise to never release Xbox exclusive titles on rival platforms.
After leaked splash art fanned rumors that Xbox hastily decided to cancel a Gears of War: E-Day PS5 port, the company said it did not make any "last-minute" decisions when it comes to its platform choice. While Searcy said it brought The Coalition joy to see their new game leading Microsoft's renewed interest in exclusive titles, making sure they made a great game was what came first.
"I think this is true of most game devs: You're just passionate about your craft," he said. "We're all gamers first and foremost. We love making games. We love making Gears. So, from our perspective, we just wanted to make the best goddamn Gears game we could. We wanted it to be a technical and art showpiece, and I think getting to see Asha on-stage say, 'To return to Xbox, we're returning to Gears,' yeah, that's a really cool moment.
He continued: "We know how much Xbox means to a lot of people. We're proud to be one of Xbox's main titles – I think it's been that way for a long time – and it's pretty cool to show up now and fill that role again."
Gears of War: E-Day launched in early access for Premium Edition players on PC and Xbox Series X/S October 1, 2026. Its full launch will follow this week, October 6. IGN's early review, which covered only the campaign mode, returned a 9/10. The game's story director was laid off just one week before it made its way to players' hands a few days ago. Now, more developers at The Coalition is bracing for additional layoffs.

item.title: Wallhacks have plagued Call of Duty for years, but in Modern Warfare 4, Activision has a plan to change that.
item.description:
Wallhacks have plagued Call of Duty for years, but in Modern Warfare 4, Activision has a plan to change that.
If you're unfamiliar with the term, wallhacks are a type of cheat that allows nefarious players to see their opponents' every move through walls. Call of Duty is far from the only multiplayer-centric gaming franchise to suffer from cheaters who use the tool, but it might be the most infamous example – and in Modern Warfare 4, that's all about to change.
As detailed in a new video published on the franchise's official social media pages, publisher Activision and developer Infinity Ward revealed a new system aimed at combating wallhack cheaters. Called "server culling," the goal is to make Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 more reliable – and fair – than ever before.
Few things ruin a great match faster than wondering whether an opponent earned the win or saw you through a wall.Wallhacks give cheaters information they were never meant to have. With Modern Warfare 4, we’re introducing a new way to fight back: Server Culling.Here’s how it… pic.twitter.com/62m41zMbLa
The relatively in-depth explanation touches on how cheaters have been able to use wallhacks thus far. Usually, servers share information, such as a player's in-game location, between game clients. It means that, even when you can't see an enemy hiding behind cover, waiting to pop out for an easy kill, the game itself still recognizes that the player is there.
Server culling, which saw Infinity Ward build occlusion layers into Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's environments, essentially limits information to what the player is able to see. So, if you can't see someone behind the wall, the backend can't either – and that goes for wallhackers, too.
"For legitimate players, the match plays exactly as intended," Activision explained. "For cheat developers, this creates a major new obstacle."
Server culling will touch every multiplayer map available in Modern Warfare 4 when launch arrives, but it doesn't stop there. Call of Duty's new take on DMZ, the Combat Outpost mode, Warzone, and future updates will benefit from this attack on wallhacks, too. All of this new tech works alongside pre-existing anti-cheat methods across all platforms, too.
Activision said it expects server culling to "disturb the cheat marketplace," but it won't "sit on our hands" when it comes to improving the overall experience going forward. There are plenty of different ways for cheaters to disrupt the experience for the average player, and while cheat manufacterers will no doubt look for new ways to learn from Activision's advancements, the publisher said it will do its best to stay on top of the issue.
"Cheat software can’t reveal information it never receives," the Call of Duty team explained in a follow-up post. "When a player shouldn’t be able to know where an opponent is, the server can now withhold that opponent’s location data from their hardware. It’s a new layer in the fight for fair play, working alongside the rest of our anti-cheat systems Server Culling will cover every map available at launch for MW4."
See you at launch, we'll keep at it
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S October 23, 2026. How fans will rank it amongst other installments in the franchise remains to be seen, but with changes to 2XP tokens and a villain played by Death Stranding and Casino Royale actor Mads Mikkelsen, it's clear the developers have put in the work to get players interested.
For more, you can read up on how the series' anti-cheat boss pushed back on some cheating myths. You can also check out how much Activision estimated the cheating market generates per year.

item.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi said he did his best to fight for a disc release as the industry heads toward a "future where physical media is essentially disc-less."
item.description:
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi said he did his best to fight for a disc release as the industry heads toward a "future where physical media is essentially disc-less."
The lead developer in charge of next year's new remake chapter opened up about the state of gaming during an interview with Radio Times. It's a topic he's touched on before, but this time, he explained how his own appreciation for physical media led him to push for Final Fantasy 7 Revelation to get at least one disc as the industry speeds toward an all-digital future.
"Personally, obviously, I bought lots of physical editions of games as a child. Sometimes I buy digital editions of games, but if I'm particularly attached to a title, I want to get the physical version," Hamaguchi said, noting how the topic of a fully digital future has become "particularly sensitive" in recent months. "And you know, being in the industry, sometimes I want to get my friends or acquaintances who've worked on something to sign a copy of their own game."
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is confirmed to have a disc option when it launches in 2027, but there are some caveats. When physical owners on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, for example, pop their discs in, they should know the full experience will require an additional download – and a hefty one at that. It's a decision that has some fans split, but not one Hamaguchi and the team at Square Enix took lightly.
"I do really like and appreciate physical media," he said. "I see a lot of people on social media saying, 'No disc, no purchase,' and I understand where they're coming from."
Hamaguchi acknowledged that Final Fantasy 7 Revelation does have a disc alternative for those who want it, even if it's just a "key disc" that only has "the opening." He added that he understands that "there are people out there with a lot of opinions" about the future of physical media and shared a message to those who feel most passionately about the issue.
"First of all, I've got people saying to me on social media, 'Give us a full disc version!' And so, from an overall perspective, let me first say that as the director, it's my responsibility to look after the content of the game to make sure it's fun, really exciting," he said. Then, smiling, he added, "The product line-up, the SKUs (stock keeping units), how it's going on sale; that is the responsibility of the publishing team. So, my authority there is somewhat limited."
Despite the "pressure" for disc-less editions and digital editions, Hamaguchi said he "used my position to put forth an argument for the physical version as much as possible." That resulted in negotiations, "both internally and with first parties," leading to Final Fantasy 7 Revelation's one-disc strategy. He added, "I completely understand there are those out there who may not really agree with that direction or approve of that direction," but it's what he fought for, and it's the best result he could conjure.
"I completely understand there are those out there who may not really agree with that direction or approve of that direction," he said. "But I would just say that I hope you understand that I completely see where you're coming from, and that I did my best."
He added with a laugh, "It is a very tricky subject."
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will release with a disc when it releases for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S April 8, 2027. Although its launch strategy hasn't pleased everyone, it's a date that will see it arrive months before PlayStation phases out physical releases for new PS5 games. Even after Rockstar signaled changing times when it announced a disc-less release for Grand Theft Auto 6, Sony's decision sent shockwaves through the industry.
Gaming fans have expected an all-digital future to arrive at some point, but it seems to be here sooner than most expected. Elsewhere in the interview, Hamaguchi said he thinks "physical media will remain in some form going forward," but it's impossible to deny that change is coming.
"But the PC market, for example, is going from strength to strength, and lots of people already purchase digital copies of games and just download them.
"So, I can see a world in the not-too-distant future where physical media is essentially disc-less. You would have a copy of the code on a piece of paper inside the physical box or something like that."
For more on why the Square Enix team chose to approach Final Fantasy 7 Revelation's physical release the way it did, you can see Hamaguchi's explanation here. You can also read more about the director's love for physical media.

item.title: The official social media account for the popular RPG-dating sim Love and Deepspace issued a warning to players after announcing some fictional cocktails with potentially disastrous real-world consequences if actually consumed.
item.description:
The official social media account for the popular RPG-dating sim Love and Deepspace issued a warning to players after announcing some fictional cocktails with potentially disastrous real-world consequences if actually consumed.
On September 28, Love and Deepspace revealed five ‘Shimmering Blend’ cocktail recipes as part of an in-game event, each themed around one of the game’s dashing romanceable characters. While they’re pretty to look at, you shouldn’t actually make some of these, as they include garnishes that are poisonous to humans.
For example, one of these drinks is made of pomegranate juice, with a garnish of cinnamon and datura. Another features sweet peach juice with a flame lily garnish and gelatin sheets.
There’s nothing wrong with peach and pomegranate juice, but these floral garnishes are making some players anxious that a fan might actually try to out the recipes themselves. Datura is a highly poisonous plant and is considered psychoactive; when consumed, it produces side effects like delirium, fever, tachychardia, and hallucinations.
Flame Lilies are also dangerous, as all parts of the plant contain a chemical called colchicine; while it’s used for medicinal purposes, it can be lethal, causing symptoms like fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and even hypovolemic shock, which causes the loss of lethal amounts of blood and bodily fluids.
It didn’t take long for concerned fans to point out these dangerous plants, fearing that some players might try their hand at making the cocktails for real. Commenters flooded the replies with calls for the Love and Deepspace account to delete the post completely, with one writing, “Delete this. This is literal poison. Nobody make this.”
Safety Notice: All drinks shown are fictional and for in-game purposes only. Do not attempt to recreate or consume them in reality.
“Hey, so some of these flowers are literally poisonous. Be careful. This is so reckless to post this,” another said.
"Don't try to recreate these drinks, they contain toxic plants!" yet another warned. "I can't believe this is posted as 'recipes.'"
Not long after, the LaDS account added a follow-up post with a safety notice, which reads: “All drinks shown are fictional and for in-game purposes only. Do not attempt to recreate or consume them in reality.”
In addition to calls from fans to delete the posts, the LaDS social media accounts continue to be flooded with photos of canceled love interest Valko, who was announced and subsequently canned before he was even released. This prompted an impressive movement from the game’s playerbase, who created shrines to the character and even gathered outside the developer’s physical offices to make their voices heard.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Resident Evil and Street Fighter developer Capcom revealed some big changes coming to its RE Engine, which they plan to gradually improve and transform into an "AI-generation game engine."
item.description:
Resident Evil and Street Fighter developer Capcom revealed some big changes coming to its RE Engine, which they plan to incrementally improve and transform into an "AI-generation game engine."
On October 2, Capcom held its own tech conference, called ‘Capcom Open Conference RE: 2026.’ One of the most notable takeaways from this event was a presentation given by programmer Satoshi Ishida, titled ‘The Outlook and Future of the REX Project, Further Evolving the RE Engine for the Next Generation.’ The purpose of this presentation was to outline several major changes coming to the RE Engine, which will come in the form of a multi-step improvement project called ‘REX.’
As reported by Japanese news outlet GameBiz, Ishida mentioned three major issues that Capcom is currently experiencing when it comes to game development: First, games are now so massive that simple processes have become extremely time-consuming; increased numbers of staff mean an engine is needed that’s easy for everyone to use; and finally, “successfully integrating AI technology into development workflows has become an essential condition for streamlining future development.”
GameBiz’s report confirmed that REX was created to help solve these problems by improving the efficiency of game development, game performance, tools, quality assurance, etc. Capcom felt that, rather than creating a brand-new engine from scratch, gradually adding these improvements over time is the best way to help evolve the RE Engine to the next generation.
We won’t get into the weeds of all the specific improvements included in the REX program, but Capcom is making at least some of them open-source for the purpose of training AI. Most interestingly, AI plays into Capcom’s larger, long-term goal of turning the RE Engine into an “AI-generation game engine” using its REX improvements.
GameBiz stated that REX unifies the entire RE Engine system under the “world’s most common programming language," meaning that it’s equal parts easier for humans to use and for AI to understand. Capcom’s goal is to build a future where it “creates games together with AI”; keeping REX in mind, this seems to mean that Capcom is utilizing artificial intelligence to speed up and streamline certain processes to make development easier, not necessarily to generate assets or artworks wholesale.
In the past, Capcom has been publicly averse to using AI to create assets, but confirmed that it will use artificial intelligence as a tool for optimizing how it makes games.
“We will not implement assets generated by AI into our games.” Capcom said in a March 2026 shareholders meeting. “However, we plan to proactively use it as a contributing technology to improve the efficiency and productivity of the game development process. To this end, we are currently exploring ways to implement it in various areas, including graphics, sound and programming."
This is the latest big news to come from Capcom after Resident Evil executive producer Jun Takeuchi revealed that plans are already in place to prepare the series for when RE remakes catch up to modern games, saying the series is being developed along “two tracks.”
It’s been a big year for the company; this year alone, Capcom has produced three critically-acclaimed titles in Resident Evil Requiem, Pragmata, and Onimusha: Way of the Sword, alongside two movie adaptations in Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil and Legendary’s Street Fighter flick, set to release in theaters on October 16, 2026.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Former NFL coach Mike Tomlin spent 19 seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers and won Super Bowl LXIII, and now he's added another major accomplishment to his resume: becoming a Minecraft YouTuber.
item.description:
Former NFL coach Mike Tomlin spent 19 seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers and won Super Bowl LXIII, and now he's added another major accomplishment to his resume: becoming a Minecraft YouTuber.
The former coach gave football fans a little something different when he launched his new YouTube channel earlier this week. With a profile picture taken in front of NBC's Football Night in America logo, watchers probably weren't expecting Tomlin's first upload to see him confess how his love for architecture and family led him to work on a Minecraft city he spent 12 years building.
"You know, 12 or 13 years ago, when my kids were in middle school, they'd be in their room all weekend and have friends over. They were obsessed with playing this game, Minecraft, that I knew nothing about," he explained as his son and channel operator, Dino, sat in the background. "I got interested because I just was mesmerized by what could occupy their attention for such large periods of time."
He admitted he lacked the "stick control" to handle something like Minecraft's Survival mode but still managed to find enjoyment in Creative Mode. That's where Mojang's systems really started to click.
"I like to build," he said. "I've always had an interest in architecture, and so forth, so I started doing this creative city. It was a means of spending time with them. They participated all over this city. All my kids have buildings."
However, as his kids went off to high school and college, their interest in Minecraft waned. For Tomlin, it was just beginning. In 2026, after 12 years of building, the sandbox phenomenon has become therapeutic for the former NFL coach, and what he's built has the internet in disbelief.
"This is where it all started for me," Tomlin said as a blocky blue pond surrounded by detailed city buildings faded into view. His tour then begins with a closer look at a hotel. This one building features a fully fleshed-out interior with labeled rooms, a lobby, a ballroom, a pool, bathrooms, and more. Tomlin even factored in how lighting might affect the views in some of these rooms – and that's just one of many locations he's made.
"I was always inspired," he added. "I'd go places, and I'd see things and buildings, and I get inspired, I go home, and I work on it."
Tomlin then referenced the off-campus housing around universities that he recreated after dropping Dino off at college. The color, floor plans, and other memorable elements all came from these memories, with much of his creation also built around different bodies of water.
Tomlin stepped down as the Steelers' coach in January 2026, with today's video showing how he's spent at least some of the downtime since. He spent years in the NFL, but it's his work as a Minecraft YouTuber that has everyone talking today.
Mike Tomlin has been working on his Minecraft world for over a decade It’s UNREAL pic.twitter.com/XWxu9zMinY
Aaron Rodgers: “CALL THE F*CKING PLAY!”Mike McCarthy: “F*cking asshole”*Loses to the Cleveland Browns*Meanwhile, Mike Tomlin: pic.twitter.com/axnE3655rT
Steelers down 20 in a playoff game.Mike Tomlin: pic.twitter.com/J4u56digNW
Mike Tomlin leaving the presser early to go finish building the Executive Spa in his Minecraft world pic.twitter.com/yHF2FOzeiZ
"I'm obsessed why is he genuinely a better builder than me," content creator @Krtzyy said.
"Mike Tomlin becoming a Minecraft YouTuber was not on my bingo card for 2026," one X/Twitter user said.
Tomlin signed off, promising to take a closer look at his city in future videos. He also teased plans to show off something that "I think you're going to find interesting." Despite being maybe the most creative celebrity gamer to come out of 2026, the ex-NFL coach isn't the only notable name to share their love for gaming in the last year. Obsession breakout Inde Navarrette garnered attention for her The Last of Us and Call of Duty streams a few months ago. Newly announced X-Men star, Samara Weaving, is also a big gamer.
Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images.

item.title: Disney has responded after rumors suggested it was interested in buying Fortnite developer Epic Games.
item.description:
Disney has responded after rumors suggested it was interested in buying Fortnite developer Epic Games.
Disney president and chief creative officer Dana Walden touched on the company's relationship with Epic during an interview with Bloomberg Live. When asked if there have been talks about expanding their previously established relationship with a full-on acquisition, she said that strategy isn't something Disney is entertaining, at least right now.
"Well, I think that it was pretty obvious that we had very serious conversations about an investment and an equity stake," Walden responded. "Those are not the conversations we're having right now, but we have a great partnership and a number of launches coming up over the next two years that are going to demonstrate the value of this partnership."
The relationship referenced here was solidified when Disney announced it acquired a $1.5 billion stake in Epic back in early 2024. It was a massive play that it promised would result in collaborations across Fortnite and more in the future.
"Our exciting new relationship with Epic Games will bring together Disney’s beloved brands and franchises with the hugely popular Fortnite in a transformational new games and entertainment universe," then-CEO Bob Iger said. "This marks Disney’s biggest entry ever into the world of games and offers significant opportunities for growth and expansion. We can’t wait for fans to experience the Disney stories and worlds they love in groundbreaking new ways."
We're still feeling the shockwaves of that deal, but some suspected it could evolve into more than a simple partnership. Tech reporter Alex Heath said in March 2026 that some Disney executives were "waiting for that moment" to go all in on an acquisition. Then, in April, Bloomberg reported that Epic was working on an extraction shooter featuring Disney characters with plans to launch in November 2026.
We're now kicking off October with no official mention of that unannounced project, but that doesn't mean Disney x Epic is going anywhere any time soon. While an acquisition isn't in the cards, Walden's promise regarding "a number of launches" set to arrive in the next few years suggests there is plenty more to talk about.
We'll have to wait and see how the two entertainment giants work together moving forward. In the meantime, you can read some of the other ways Disney and Epic have bolstered their relationship, including a Disneyland-exclusive Fortnite skin and officially licensed Star Wars minigames.

item.title: Dan Houser, the former co-boss of Rockstar Games and former creative director on the Grand Theft Auto series, doesn't play a lot of open-world games. And he doesn't plan on playing GTA 6 either. But it's for a good creative reason: he doesn't want to be influenced by them as he works on his two new game projects at his new enterprise, Absurd Ventures.
item.description:
Dan Houser, the former co-boss of Rockstar Games and former creative director on the Grand Theft Auto series, doesn't play a lot of open-world games. And he doesn't plan on playing GTA 6 either. But it's for a good creative reason: he doesn't want to be influenced by them as he works on his two new game projects at his new enterprise, Absurd Ventures.
"Given that I spend a large amount of time trying to make open-world games, and the rest of my conscious time trying to figure out innovative ways to market them, I don’t need to see what other people are [doing]," he told Variety. I’m always trying to think about new ways of doing it, not sit there in some kind of comparison of what I would have done differently."
"It’s not my job within any company that I’ve ever worked at, thankfully, to be the person that understands what everyone else is doing," Houser continued. "I’m trying to think about new ways of doing it. So when we worked on Red Dead Redemption, as soon as we started working, I never watched another Western. I never watched The Sopranos until after I left Rockstar. I saw one episode, because my girlfriend-now-wife and I did watch the finale in real time. I’d not seen any of it before that moment. And then I watched it all during COVID. And I’m grateful. It’s so good that it would have disrupted everything I did on GTA, had I watched at the time. So I really try and avoid things that I think are going to overly influence me."
On not playing many other open-world games, Houser said, "I find when I play them, I can almost deconstruct the strengths and weaknesses of the team in real time and it’s distracting. I’m always thinking, ‘Well, their animation team is weak, but I think this game design is fantastic.’ And, ‘Oh, I can imagine that meeting when they discuss this feature.’ I’m not a game designer, I’m a sort of creative director. So I’m trying to always find new things that haven’t been done before, or that I can steal from older media, quite frankly or just inspired me or things I always thought about."
Houser's new company, Absurd Ventures, is currently working on two games, as discussed in my all-too-brief conversation with him at LA Comic-Con last year. The studio has already released American Caper, a graphic novel series. Its double-sized season-finale issue drops next month – a week before GTA 6 – along with the book "A Better Paradise."
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: GTA 6 has received a rating of PEGI 18, revealing mentions of "decapitation," the ability for players to snort cocaine at any time, "scenes of sexual fetishes," and much more.
item.description:
UPDATE October 2, 2026, 11:39 a.m. PT: PEGI has seemingly updated its website to remove the age rating for GTA 6.
The PEGI 18 page – which, as viewed by IGN, included what appeared to be new details about GTA 6 – is no longer available. In its place is a blank listing that says, "The requested page could not be found." Users on X/Twitter have captured and shared an image of the listing and have continued to share its contents across social media. IGN has reached out to PEGI for comment.
Grand Theft Auto VI PEGI rating is now up!https://t.co/av3HXd6GQf pic.twitter.com/6MhVcAA1xc
ORIGINAL STORY: GTA 6 has received an age rating of PEGI 18, revealing mentions of "decapitation," the ability for players to snort cocaine at any time, "scenes of sexual fetishes," and much more.
The update, which can be found on the Pan European Game Information board's website, gives players a relatively in-depth description of Rockstar Games' megaton video game ahead of its launch in November. The PEGI 18 rating arrives just one day after GTA 6 received its official ESRB rating, which, also unsurprisingly, resulted in an "M for Mature."
GTA 6's rating describes a story that allows players to take control of "Jason Duval or Lucia Caminos, two criminals who become involved in a criminal conspiracy following a failed robbery." It adds that they'll work together as "they become increasingly entangled in criminal activities" in Vice City, with gameplay that, as we've already seen, is par for the course when it comes to Grand Theft Auto.
What's different about GTA 6 is the unprecedented detail Rockstar has shoved into the game, with previous footage showing off an open-world sandbox with enough activities to make up for the 13-year wait. PEGI dived into that, too, but there are still even more new highlights to go over.
The board described the game's violence as "bloody with a high degree of realism." Some weapons will be more brutal than others, with some said to be "able to cause greater damage, such as detailed decapitation and dismemberment." This time around, Rockstar has made drug use "frequent and prominent," with players able to partake in illicit substances. Cocaine is said to be especially important in Vice City, with the rating promising that Jason and Lucia will be able to use the substance directly from their inventory, as it can be "snorted directly from their hand at any time."
The GTA 6 PEGI description also touched on "strong sexual themes," which include "nudity, scenes of intercourse, and occasional scenes of sexual fetishes." It's a lot that we knew and some details that we didn't, but you can read the "content specific issues" section of the summary in its entirety below.
"This game contains frequent depictions of violence; due to the free roam nature of the game the player can harm all other characters inhabiting the environment," PEGI said. "This includes civilians, criminals and the authorities. Violence is bloody with a high degree of realism, with certain weapons being able to cause greater damage such as detailed decapitation and dismemberment.
"Drug use is frequent and prominent with the player being able to partake in drug use with others and to use illegal drugs directly from their inventory. Most notably, cocaine can be carried around by the player and snorted directly from their hand at any time.
"There are also strong sexual themes, including nudity, scenes of intercourse and occasional scenes of sexual fetishes. In various night clubs the player can also pay for private dances, during which, the game allows the player to move their hands onto the dancers’ breasts and buttocks."
The PEGI age rating also mentioned "other issues," including that domestic animals can be harmed, though not in the same detail as humans. The word "f**k" is also featured prominently in the game, while the word "c**t" is only occasionally featured. The description also said that "discriminatory language can be heard in the TV shows and on the radio channels."
Finally, GTA 6 reminds players that they will have the option to purchase in-game items, though it's still unclear what this entails. In August, it was reported that Rockstar would not include microtransactions or generative AI in the game.
GTA 6 is still on course to launch for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19, 2026. You can read more about how Rockstar has ramped up its marketing tactics here, and you can see what we learned from some new screenshots here. While we wait for any more updates, you can read IGN's interview and preview.

item.title: Disney plans to license a mix of legacy titles and currently-streaming TV shows to Netflix as part of a new deal between the two firms. In the deal, Netflix will host select Disney content for its 325 million subscribers.
item.description:
Disney plans to license Ice Age, Percy Jackson and more to Netflix as part of a new deal between the two firms.
In the deal, Netflix will host select Disney+ content for its 325 million subscribers, including a mix of legacy titles and currently streaming TV shows. The deal is designed to help boost interest in contemporary Disney series such as Percy Jackson and the Olympians, which joins Netflix on October 4. The first two seasons will appear on the rival streaming platform ahead of its Disney+ Season 3 premiere on November 20.
All five 20th Century Studios’ Ice Age movies will land on Netflix at the same time as Percy Jackson. Will Trent Seasons 1-4, Shifting Gears Seasons 1-2, and Tracker Seasons 1-3 are also heading to Netflix between November this year and February 2027.
In 2027, a range of Walt Disney Animation and Pixar movies will also head to Netflix, including Soul, Elio, and Raya and the Last Dragon, along with a selection of complete series such as Felicity, This is Us, Revenge, and Fresh off the Boat. Release dates for these vary by region.
According to the Variety exclusive, this will be a mutually beneficial deal, with Netflix getting more content and Disney getting more eyes on the kind of things it offers outside of its biggest franchise titles (and presumably some cash).
Those franchise titles such as Marvel and Star Wars will remain exclusive to Disney+, keeping its Disney-branded titles as the main selling point of the subscription service. Netflix will also continue to invest in its own content, with original series and animations such as Arcane, The Witcher, and Castlevania keeping subscribers fed.
Netflix recently announced its streaming lineup for October, which includes miniseries East of Eden, Ben Affleck’s Animals, and Josh Hartnett squaring off against a sea beast in Below.
Disney+ has an exciting October coming up too, featuring Marvel’s VisionQuest, horrible (in a good way) horror movie Barbarian, and American Horror Story: 13. With Disney+ and Hulu merging their libraries, there’s more choice than ever over there.
It’s just a shame Disney+ had to increase its pricing again ahead of the next big Marvel drop. It’s a bit of a Thor point. If you can’t afford subscriptions to Netflix and Disney, though, at least you’ll be able to catch some Disney+ stuff on Netflix from October 4.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: DC Studios co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran will seemingly keep their vision for the DCU alive following the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger.
item.description:
UPDATE October 2, 2026, 12:22 p.m. PT: Skydance's David Ellison reportedly told James Gunn and Peter Safran to "keep doing what you're doing" at a meeting that took place earlier this week.
The Hollywood Reporter's sources say the two moviemakers are staying right where they are "at least for the foreseeable future" after they had a positive meeting with Ellison yesterday. They were both invited to stay, with one source saying that Ellison asked them to simply "keep doing what you're doing." He also allegedly visited the Man of Tomorrow set in Atlanta earlier this summer.
Who the two DC Studios CEOs will report to in the immediate future, however, is less clear. Deadline also corroborated reports that Gunn and Safran will continue to build out their DCU as the merger is finalized.
ORIGINAL STORY: DC Studios co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran will seemingly keep their vision for the DCU alive following the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger.
Rumors that the two comic book movie executives would be shuffled out amidst the tumultuous merger have swirled for months. Now, as the $110 billion deal comes to a close under its new Skydance banner, it seems Gunn and Safran – as well as the cinematic universe that includes projects like 2025's Superman and Lanterns – are safe.
Puck has reported that both creatives "will be invited to stay on at DC, at least initially" as all the moving pieces come together behind the scenes. What the long-term future holds remains to be seen, but it sounds like more DC movies and shows will continue to fall in line as the DCU navigates its early ups and downs.
Adding weight to the continuation of the current iteration of the DC universe is Gunn himself. After that new Skydance title was announced, the former Marvel director took to Instagram to celebrate the news by sharing its flashy new trailer. Included amongst the cuts of Paramount and Warner Bros. logos are shots from Superman, Robert Pattinson's The Batman, and even the DC logo itself.
"What once was the peak, is now just the beginning," Gunn, echoing the trailer, said in the post's caption.
Gunn and Safran officially took over the DC entertainment business in 2022 and will continue to oversee it – at least through 2027. That's when their contracts are set to expire, and while there are plenty of other projects set to release before then, whether they'll choose to renew under new leadership remains to be seen.
In the meantime, the DCU charges ahead. After Superman started things off with a bang and Supergirl failed to live up expectations, the cinematic universe is just days away from airing the Lanterns Season 1 finale. The Green Lantern introduction series has received praise from critics and fans thanks to strong casting choices in Kyle Chandler as Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre as John Stewart. Next up for this month is a theatrical release in Batman body horror spinoff, Clayface.
Next year, The Last Son of Krypton will find his way to the big screen once again when Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow premieres in July. With Xolo Maridueña already set to return as Blue Beetle and fans hoping to see Adira Arjona play a new take on Wonder Woman, it's clear there's still room for the DCU to grow.
For more as we wait to see what Gunn and Safran have planned for the future, you can read about the Mr. Terrific TV show that's said to be in the works. You can also see what Pattinson had to say about theories that his Batman may cross over with David Corenswet's Man of Steel.

item.title: Rockstar has further ramped up its GTA 6 marketing today with the launch of several new screenshots focusing on protagonists Lucia and Jason.
item.description:
Rockstar has further ramped up its GTA 6 marketing today with the launch of several new screenshots focusing on protagonists Lucia and Jason.
GTA 6's dynamic criminal duo can be seen in four new images published via Love Magazine, which features an illustration of the couple on its cover, and a black-and-white screenshot of the pair in more casual clothes (Jason in a white vest, jacked arms on show, Lucia in a leopard-print crop top).
Two more images show Lucia and Jason together in the booth of a diner, but sat opposite. Is this the setting of a heist planning session, or are the two about to hold-up the very diner they're sat in? Are they having a date, or an argument about the way their criminal undertakings are going? What looks like a large bag set to be filled with stolen money suggests something is afoot.
Next up are images of Lucia and Jason in more stylish clothes (well, Jason is in bike leathers), and looking fierce while playing pool in what appears to be a biker bar.
The article also includes further detail from Rockstar senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, who discussed the pair's pursuit of the American Dream. GTA 6 portrays this as the couple seeking the ability to own a house and pay off their various debts, rather than a desire to become billionaires. “If you are going to put all this effort into creating a version of today’s world, it has to be more over the top, more insane, more in your face,” Humphries said. “Otherwise, you could just go outside and live in the real world.”
"We wanted both protagonists to be vulnerable, tough, flawed, right sometimes, wrong sometimes, able to learn from each other,” game writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern told Love. “That’s what we felt made them authentic, and a great team.” Game writer Alexa D’Agostino added: “When you are focusing on writing a fully realised person with their own wants, you’re going to get something perfectly imperfect — with clichés, but also undeniably real.”
Speaking of GTA 6 marketing ramping up, The Miami Heat announced it would be heading to Vice City for its next NBA match against the Milwaukee Bucks. The one-night-only event, hosted live on ESPN, has been dubbed A Night in Vice City, and will see the home team donning an "all-new uniform on a never-before-seen court."
We've got extensive coverage of GTA 6 across IGN. Check out IGN's interview with Rockstar Games, our GTA 6 preview, and word of the first confirmed GTA 6 voice actor.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Pokémon TCG is reportedly launching its first-ever Valentine's Day box set on January 27, 2027, featuring mini packs and packaging that folds into a classroom mailbox.
item.description:
The Pokémon Company is intending to launch the franchise's very first dedicated Valentine's Day collection on January 27, 2027, according to a recent report from Pokébeach.
While the Valentine set is yet to be officially confirmed, the leaks reportedly suggest that the "Pokémon TCG Valentine’s Box" will be similar in practice to the popular Trick or Trade Halloween series, rather than a full expansion release like Pokémon TCG's Delta Reign or Chaos Rising expansions.
These seasonal sets typically come in compact foil packs containing three cards, alongside sticker sheets. The Halloween releases were given their own pumpkin-stamped Pikachu, so I'd put good money on the Valentine's version getting some kind of suitably pink Pika stamp.
The Trick or Trade range was originally designed as a way for kids to hand out Pokémon cards while trick-or-treating, effectively giving them a Pokémon-themed alternative to candy. Given how expensive some Halloween sweets have become, perhaps the cards aren't such a bad substitute.
The reported Valentine's Box appears to be taking a similar approach, with the packaging and packs seemingly designed around giving cards to friends or handing them out in the classroom. The box is also apparently designed to fold into a little cardboard mailbox, allowing cards to be handed out to classmates in the same way kids might exchange Valentine's cards at school.
That's a cute idea, although given the current state of the Pokémon TCG market, I'm not entirely convinced every box will make it into the hands of an actual child.
Previous seasonal releases have generally focused on reprinted cards rather than introducing a bunch of new full-art cards, but that hasn't stopped sealed products from holding surprisingly strong secondary-market value. The Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle (last seen in 2025), for example, contains 40 mini packs with three cards apiece, and currently has a market value of around $75.99 at TCGplayer.
That makes the potential Valentine's release one to keep an eye on, particularly if it proves to be another limited seasonal product. Previous holiday releases have sold out well ahead of launch, so the real competition could come when preorders eventually open.
There's also currently no word on which Pokémon will take centre stage in the mini set. My vote would be Enamorus, although Fairy-type Pokémon aren't currently part of the TCG's standard format... Yet.
I’d also love to see Sylveon - its pink color scheme and cute ribbons would be perfect. Plus, it evolves by friendship! Other options could be Audino and Blissey, since both are linked with care and kindness - qualities that suit Valentine's Day well- or even Pikachu in loveheart-themed clothing might also show up.
Sylveon would also be an obvious choice. Its pink colour scheme and ribbons are practically made for Valentine's Day, while the fact that it evolves through friendship feels particularly appropriate. Audino and Blissey could also fit the theme nicely given their associations with care and kindness, while a loveheart-themed Pikachu would hardly come as a surprise.
Sara Heritage is a freelance journalist for IGN, specialising in Pokémon TCG. When she's not gaming, you’ll probably find her building yet another LEGO set she absolutely did not need, or chaining ranked matches in Pokémon Champions.

item.title: For as much as World of Warcraft Forever has been making an effort to preserve the vanilla WoW experience, there are just some things in the game's history that must be added, and the quest 'Kyle's Gone Missing!' is one of them. And Blizzard just added it to Forever.
item.description:
For as much as World of Warcraft Forever has been making an effort to preserve the vanilla WoW experience, there are just some things in the game's history that must be added, and the quest 'Kyle's Gone Missing!' is one of them. And Blizzard just added it to Forever.
'Kyle's Gone Missing!' was added during the Burning Crusade expansion through a Make-a-Wish campaign in 2007 for Ezra Chatterton, who was diagnosed with brain cancer earlier that year. Chatterton, who went by the in-game name of Ephoenix, voiced the quest-giver, Ahab Wheathoof, and had his dog Kyle added to the game, which players were then tasked with finding. The quest went live in patch 2.1.2 on June 19, 2007, and has been in the game ever since.
Sadly, a little over a year later, in October 2008, Chatterton passed away at the age of 12. The quest has remained a beloved part of the game ever since, and Chatterton has also been referenced multiple times, with Blizzard re-naming the Elder of Thunderbluff (who shows up during the annual Lunar Festival) after him in Wrath of the Lich King.
But because the quest was added during The Burning Crusade, it's not part of the original game, which meant it wouldn't be in World of Warcraft Forever – even if the zone where the quest takes place is the Tauren starting zone. But, after players asked Blizzard to bring the quest to Forever, it's officially been added.
Blizzard added the patch after players asked for it in the forums, when user Nyaria posted saying, "My Husband was very sad that the Make a Wish Quest involving Kyle wasn’t in Mulgore." They even acknowledged that it doesn't fit the 'Vanilla-only' ethos, but stood by it, saying, "Yes it wasn’t added until TBC, but this is WoW: Forever, we already have new quests added in, and it was a cute little quest, and a Make a Wish addition for a poor kid."
Luckily, shortly after that thread was posted Blizzard community manager Kaivax simply posted: "We're working on it. Stay tuned." The entire rest of the thread is full of players thanking Kaivax and the rest of the Forever team for adding the quest. One player, Ikory, claimed to have been a Make-a-Wish kid who survived and thanked Blizzard in a long post, which they signed off with: "I spent 30 years in crippling pain, with a failing heart, that had to be repaired every few years. I am a survivor. I was that kid who was supposed to die. Now I have a freaken PhD. I lived. Make-A-Wish helped me have hope as a kid. I got my wish. I’m glad Ezra got his wish. Thank you Blizzard for still caring about us Make-A-Wish kids after all these years."
Now, just four days later, the quest is officially live in the World of Warcraft beta, as a part of the October 1 patch.
Johnny Cash, the Blizzard Principal Designer who added the quest, posted on X/Twitter, saying "I had the honor and privilege of bringing "Kyle's Gone Missing!" into WoW: Forever. Ezra Chatterton was an enormous WoW fan, the creator and voice actor behind Ahab Wheathoof, and the creator of Kyle. A tear was shed during this one, my friends. Rest in peace, Ezra."
The quest isn't hard to get to, especially if you start off as a Tauren. Ezra's NPC is in Bloodhoof Village, which is the first town you get to while questing in Mulgore. You can pick up the quest as soon as you hit level 5, and you'll need to hunt down plainstriders (giant ostrich-looking things) until you get Tender Strider Meat, which you will then feed Kyle to get him to return home.
It's nice to see that while Blizzard has been pretty adamant about keeping the spirit of Classic World of Warcraft alive in Forever, it's willing to add a little wiggle room to add beloved pieces of WoW history like this quest. For as much as World of Warcraft has a reputation for gold selling and general toxicity, it's moments like this that remind me just how magical this game is, and how much it means to so many people.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: System Shock 2: 25th Anniversary Remaster is currently free to claim on the Epic Games Store until October 8, 2026.
item.description:
PC players can currently pick up System Shock 2: 25th Anniversary Remaster for free on the Epic Games Store until October 8, 2026. As with all of Epic's weekly freebies, anything you claim during the window stays in your library permanently. You'll need a free Epic Games account to claim System Shock 2, and the game is played through the Epic Games Launcher.
Nightdive Studios, the team behind a string of well-regarded classic revivals such as those for Quake and Star Wars: Dark Forces, released the 25th Anniversary Remaster in June 2025.
The update keeps the original design but modernises how it looks and plays, including the following changes:
The original System Shock 2 launched back in 1999, developed by Looking Glass Studios and Irrational Games, blending together an FPS shooter with the character building of an RPG. You wake from cryosleep aboard the faster-than-light ship Von Braun in the year 2114 with no memory of who you are, and the ship is overrun by hybrid mutants and hostile robots.
Its influence is hard to overstate. Many of the people behind it went on to make the BioShock games, which are often described as a spiritual successor to System Shock 2, and the game's blend of environmental storytelling and player choice has shaped plenty of what has followed. The original title garnered a 9/10 rating when it received an updated review. Now, this Epic Games Store deal offers a free way to revisit one of the most influential games ever made.
If the remaster whets your appetite, Nightdive also released a full remake of the first System Shock on PC in 2023, rebuilt with new HD visuals, updated controls and a revamped hacking system. It's a handy way to explore the series' roots, though System Shock 2 works perfectly well as a standalone adventure – that's currently $11.99 on Steam with a hefty 70% discount during the Autumn Sale.
Epic is also giving away Buried Stars this week, so it's worth heading to the store for both. It's an anime-style visual novel in which a group of contestants on a TV show must survive a mysterious attack. Like System Shock 2, it's available to claim until 8 October, and you can add both games to your library in a couple of clicks.

He's been featured in Trusted Reviews, PC Gamer, PCGamesN, Custom PC magazine, TechRadar, Eurogamer and The Guardian. He also has his own blog, UNTITLED. He is a mechanical keyboard nerd, so you'll usually find him tinkering there when not writing, or bellowing at virtual footballers on Football Manager.

item.title: The Miami Heat is heading to Vice City for its next NBA match against the Milwaukee Bucks.
item.description:
The Miami Heat is heading to Vice City for its next NBA match against the Milwaukee Bucks. The one-night-only event, hosted live on ESPN, has been dubbed A Night in Vice City, and will see the home team donning an “all-new uniform on a never-before-seen court.”
Presumably, this means the team is sponsored by Take-Two and Rockstar Games for a GTA 6 marketing stunt. As they go, this is one of the cooler ones.
The event will take place at the Kaseya Center at 7pm EST/ 4pm PT on November 18, the day before GTA launches. A bunch of fancy crossover merch has also appeared on the Miami Heat store, celebrating Vice City.
Yesterday, the top of the Kaseya Center, home of The Heat, was lit up to usher in the collaboration between Rockstar and Miami’s home team. This followed a lengthy negotiation with local officials over the extent to which Rockstar could use Miami as a base for creative advertising.
GTA 6 takes place in Leonida, a fictional recreation of Florida housing its jewel, a virtual recreation of Miami called Vice City. In-game, the Kaseya Center is dubbed the Sahara Arena.
Other studios are taking notice of what Rockstar is doing in the lead-up to launch. Earlier, one of the founders of the studio behind Kingdom Come: Deliverance held up GTA 6’s pricing as a potential turning point for the industry and video game prices in general.
Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick previously commented on GTA 6’s price speculation, saying: “Consumers pay for the value that you bring to them, and our job is to charge way way way less of the value delivery.
GTA 6 costs $79.99 for the Standard Edition. The Ultimate Edition, which includes extra in-game content, costs $99.99. GTA 6 releases for PS5 and Xbox Series consoles on November 19.
We've got extensive coverage of GTA 6 across IGN. Check out IGN's interview with Rockstar Games, our GTA 6 preview, and word of the first confirmed GTA 6 voice actor.
